source_acquisition.search_note: The PDF explicitly links https://github.com/ZhouYuxuanYX/Hierarchical-Speculative-Decoding on p. 1. Read-only gh inspection confirmed the paper title/README relationship; the only default branch is main and its tree has no paper-specific plot*, figure*, visual*, table*, .tex, .tikz, .pgf or .svg source. The acquired chain-of-thought-hub/notebooks/visualization.ipynb is a generic Minerva/PaLM/LLaMA model-scale and MMLU notebook unrelated to Figures 1, 2 or A.1 and Tables 1–4/A.1–A.4, so it is excluded. gh exact-title repository and code searches returned no additional source candidate. The repository contains implementation/results/data but no validated paper visual source.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Tables and Figure 2 are grayscale/black-and-white. Figure 1 uses a local pastel process palette (pale blue field, blue draft nodes, pale yellow resampled node, purple backward arrows, pink reject markers, mustard resampling arrow and black dashed path). Figure A.1 uses unrelated gray/sky-blue/salmon bars. No method color role persists across objects.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Body text, rules, tables and Figure 2 text/rounded boxes are vector PDF objects. Figure 1 is a mixed composition with multiple embedded RGB/soft-mask image XObjects on p. 2 at about 491 ppi plus vector text/geometry. Figure A.1 is a 600 × 400 RGB image with soft mask at about 364 ppi. There is no paper-specific public source for either raster asset.
paper_style.style_consistency: Captions and tables follow a restrained ICLR serif/booktabs-like system, but Figure 1 uses imported diagram fonts and pastel icons, Figure 2 uses a monospaced output panel, and Figure A.1 uses a small matplotlib-style raster chart. Main tables are much denser than appendix tables; the cross-object variation remains legible but is not a single plotting system.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Overview of HSD. HSD accepts the draft Xτ by scanning backward from γ to τ, and then performs a single resampling at position τ + 1 using the corresponding distribution from the resampling hierarchy.

color.semantic_mapping: Pale blue fields identify the method canvas and accepted-prefix box; blue circles are draft tokens, pale yellow is the resampled token, purple arrows are backward operations, pink crosses are rejects, the mustard arrow is resampling/next-step action, and black dashed edges are dropped paths/text.

encodings.x: Reverse verification order from γ through τ and then the next decoding step
encodings.y: Staggered branch/state positions for accepted prefix and rejected suffix
encodings.color: Draft/resampled/reject/backward/resample roles use the local pastel palette
encodings.shape: Circular token nodes, rounded branch-state rectangles, arrowheads and cross reject icons
encodings.line: Black dashed dropped path versus colored directional operations
encodings.text: Direct labels for acceptance inequalities, token positions, operation names and τ/γ

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual method interface, not a quantitative sample. The diagram shows draft positions τ, τ+1, …, γ, acceptance tests such as hτ ≥ ητ and ht < ηt, a dropped path, and one resampling from P*res(· | X1:τ). There are no observations, denominators or uncertainty intervals.
figures.evidence_relation: p. 1 introduction frames joint verification and lossless recovery; p. 2 Figure 1 maps that claim to the backward scan and hierarchical resampling interface; §§4.2–4.3 define branch divergence/hierarchy and Algorithm 2 instantiates the single resample. Tables 1–4 and Figure A.1 provide downstream efficiency evidence. The figure is structural method evidence, not a performance estimate.
design_strengths: The accepted-prefix, rejected-suffix and backward scan are visible in one double-column view.
The right legend names all six visual roles, while direct node/edge labels preserve local reading order.
Dashed path, reject-cross icon, arrow direction and color together make the state transition explicit.
design_weaknesses: Small subscripts, inequalities and legend text are difficult at the paper scale, and raster components soften on zoom.
Draft versus resampled token identity depends mainly on fill color; grayscale and color-vision-deficient reproduction lose that distinction.
Palatino/Calibri/Times/Symbol mixing looks imported from a separate diagram tool rather than the surrounding LaTeX system.
The caption explains the high-level action but leaves probability notation and legend semantics to the graphic; no quantitative acceptance or cost is encoded.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use one cross-column process diagram for accepted prefix, rejected suffix, backward verification and corrective resampling; keep operation classes in a local legend and add line-style/shape redundancy when color carries state.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: GSM8K question with the generated prefix. The text shown is the printed output of the decoded string in Markdown format.

color.semantic_mapping: Gray title strip separates the GSM8K label, near-white body holds the printed Markdown, and dark text carries the prompt/output content.

encodings.color: Title/body gray hierarchy only; no data-variable color
encodings.shape: Rounded rectangle with a gray header band and light body
encodings.text: Markdown syntax, prose and bullet/list indentation

figures.data_and_statistics: Qualitative generated-string excerpt. It shows a GSM8K overtime-pay prompt, explanatory prose and the beginning of two numbered steps; the visible prefix stops after “Eliza worked a total of 45 hours, so”. No performance metric, denominator, sample count or uncertainty is encoded.
figures.evidence_relation: §5.4 introduces the GSM8K running example and uses Figure 2 as a human-readable context for the token/probability arrays that follow. It supports interpretability of the method example, not the losslessness or speed claims measured in Tables 1–4.
design_strengths: The gray title strip and monospaced body clearly distinguish printed Markdown output from paper prose.
Full-width layout makes the question and generated-prefix relationship readable without a legend.
The panel bridges abstract token notation to a recognizable benchmark prompt.
design_weaknesses: The excerpt is visibly truncated before the overtime calculation is complete, so it does not show a final answer or an observed accept/resample event.
Small monospaced text and long lines leave little room for larger accessible type; token boundaries and accepted-prefix status are not shown.
Gray styling is descriptive rather than semantically tied to HSD’s blue/yellow/purple process palette.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a full-width monospace output panel to ground a probabilistic method in a concrete benchmark prompt, but show complete output or mark the excerpt boundary and annotate the method event being demonstrated.

figures.label: Figure A.1

caption.text: Figure A.1: The average acceptance probability of the entire draft (τ = γ) on GSM8K.

color.semantic_mapping: Gray, sky-blue and salmon bars identify tokenwise, blockwise and ours respectively; x-axis method labels provide the direct category key.

encodings.x: Verification method category: tokenwise, blockwise, ours
encodings.y: Average full-draft acceptance probability h(X1:γ) for τ = γ, with a 1e−5 scientific-notation multiplier
encodings.color: Local method identity via gray/sky-blue/salmon bars
encodings.text: X tick labels, scientific-notation y-axis and direct value labels above bars

figures.data_and_statistics: GSM8K average acceptance probability of the full draft: approximately 5.1e−07 (tokenwise), 1.1e−05 (blockwise) and 1.8e−05 (ours), as printed above the bars. No error bars, seed count, denominator or uncertainty is shown. The linear axis compresses the tokenwise bar near zero.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix D follows Lemma 9 and Theorem 7 on expected accepted-token length and uses Figure A.1 to compare full-draft acceptance terms across tokenwise, blockwise and HSD. It is the appendix empirical bridge from the theoretical acceptance-probability decomposition to the efficiency comparisons in Table 1 and Appendix Table A.1.
design_strengths: Three methods and direct scientific-notation labels make the intended ordering immediately visible.
Categorical x labels remove the need for a legend and retain meaning in grayscale.
The minimal chart is a useful local check on the theorem-to-experiment mechanism.
design_weaknesses: The tokenwise value is nearly invisible on a linear axis, with no alternate scale or inset for the dynamic range.
Colors are not explained in the caption and are not reused elsewhere; method identity relies on bar position/text.
The inset is very small and raster-only, with no uncertainty or run/denominator information.
Lowercase “ours” is less precise than HSD and differs from table labels.
figures.reusable_pattern: A compact three-bar mechanism check with direct values can bridge theory and results; use a log/inset treatment for orders-of-magnitude differences and state aggregation/uncertainty in the caption.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Comparison of Block Efficiency (BE) and Decoding Speed (DS) across datasets and model scales. Values in parentheses show percentage improvement over Tokenwise.

tables.uncertainty: No error bars, intervals, seed dispersion or repeated-run summary. Parenthesized percentages are relative improvements over Tokenwise, not uncertainty.
tables.data_and_statistics: Three datasets (GSM8K, HumanEval, CNN/DailyMail) × three methods (Tokenwise, Blockwise, HSD) × three target scales (14B, 32B, 72B), with Block Efficiency (Token/Step) and Decoding Speed (Token/Second). Point estimates use two decimal places; relative gains in parentheses use one decimal place.
tables.evidence_relation: §6.2 Main results explicitly calls Table 1 for the HSD headline across Qwen2.5 target scales; Figure 1 gives the method interface, while Table 2 extends to multi-draft and Tables 3–4 test ablations/integration.
design_strengths: Two-level headers align the two decision metrics with model scales.
Dataset group rows and HSD bolding support fast cross-scale scanning.
Parenthetical deltas make the baseline comparison explicit without a separate gain column.
design_weaknesses: Seven columns and approximately 7 pt text are dense at normal paper size.
Parentheses compare only against Tokenwise and do not quantify uncertainty.
Runtime, accuracy and failure information are outside the table, and vertical separators partially conflict with a minimal booktabs language.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a full-width two-level metric/model header, explicit dataset group rows and bold proposal rows for a compact multi-benchmark comparison; add run dispersion or cost/quality columns when those claims matter.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Comparison of our HSD and tokenwise verification in Multi-draft setting.

tables.uncertainty: No error bars, intervals, seed dispersion or repeated-run summary. Parenthesized percentages are relative gains over Tokenwise, not uncertainty.
tables.data_and_statistics: Four rows pair single-draft Tokenwise/HSD with 11-candidate multi-draft Tokenwise/HSD across GSM8K, HumanEval and CNN/DailyMail. Block Efficiency and Decoding Speed are point estimates; parenthesized gains are relative to the corresponding Tokenwise row.
tables.evidence_relation: §6.2 Multi-draft motivates the table; Appendix G Algorithm 3 provides HSD + Recursive Reject Sampling integration. Table 1 supplies single-draft context, and Table 4a adds LLaMA-family multi-draft results.
design_strengths: Paired single-draft/multi-draft rows make compatibility easy to scan.
Repeated grouped headers keep BE and DS comparable across datasets.
The table avoids inventing Blockwise multi-draft values that the body says are not straightforward to obtain.
design_weaknesses: The caption omits K = 11/RRS and the reason Blockwise is absent.
No uncertainty, accuracy, runtime or failure information is shown.
Long method labels and six numeric columns are hard to read at the small table size.
tables.reusable_pattern: Pair baseline and extended-configuration rows under shared metric headers, and state the multi-draft protocol plus omitted-baseline boundary in the caption rather than relying on surrounding prose.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Ablations on temperature, draft length, and target model size on GSM8K. Except for the ablation on target model size, we adopt Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen2.5-72B as the draft and target pair.

tables.uncertainty: No error bars, intervals, seed dispersion or repeated-run summary; all cells are point estimates.
tables.data_and_statistics: Two side-by-side panels each contain Tokenwise, Blockwise and Hierarchical rows. Panel (a) varies temperature t = 0.6, 0.8, 1 at γ = 10; panel (b) varies draft length γ = 5, 10, 15 at t = 1. Each panel reports Block Efficiency and Decoding Speed to two decimals. The caption also names target-model-size ablation, but no such panel is visible.
tables.evidence_relation: §6.2 cites Table 3(a) for temperature robustness and 3(b) for draft-length scaling; Appendix Table A.2 checks task accuracy by target size, while Appendix E discusses capping separately.
design_strengths: Side-by-side factor panels conserve space while retaining a shared method row key.
Repeated BE/DS grouping makes temperature and draft-length effects directly comparable.
No color is needed for method identity, so the compact table remains grayscale-readable.
design_weaknesses: The caption advertises a target-model-size ablation that the visible table does not contain.
The row label “Hierarchicial” is misspelled in panel (a), while panel (b) uses “Hierarchical”.
Tiny condition headers and absent gain/dispersion encoding make practical effect size harder to judge.
The factor symbols t and γ are only locally explained by subpanel titles.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use paired small-multiple ablation panels with a shared row key and metric hierarchy, but make the caption enumerate only visible factors and highlight the factor/condition that changes the decision.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: Extended experimental results using the LLaMA model family and EAGLE-3 framework on GSM8K. Note that we replace EAGLE-3’s tokenwise verification with our HSD, yielding EAGLE-3H.

tables.uncertainty: No error bars, intervals, seed dispersion or repeated-run summary. Parenthesized percentages are relative gains, not uncertainty.
tables.data_and_statistics: Panel (a) reports Tokenwise, Blockwise and HSD on the LLaMA-3 family for single- and multi-draft Block Efficiency/Decoding Speed. Panel (b) reports EAGLE-3, Blockwise and EAGLE-3H for Block Eff. and Decoding Speed, with N/A for Blockwise. Values are point estimates; body text specifies LLaMA-3.1-70B/8B, eight H20 GPUs and γ = 7 for EAGLE-3.
tables.evidence_relation: §6.2 Extended Results calls Table 4a/4b; the replacement path is Algorithm 2/Appendix F, and Table 2 provides the preceding multi-draft comparison. The table is cross-family and integration evidence rather than the primary Qwen2.5 headline.
design_strengths: Paired panels connect model-family robustness to drop-in EAGLE integration.
Grouped headers keep single/multi-draft and BE/DS dimensions aligned.
Explicit N/A preserves the not-applicable Blockwise comparison.
design_weaknesses: Model and hardware conditions are absent from the table itself.
No uncertainty or per-run variability is shown, even though the body attributes BE differences partly to stochasticity/precision.
The two panels have different widths and scope, which weakens direct visual comparison.
tables.reusable_pattern: Place cross-family generalization and framework integration in coordinated panels, carry N/A explicitly, and put known stochastic/implementation caveats in the caption or an adjacent note.

tables.label: Table A.1

caption.text: Table A.1: Comparison of different algorithm performance on GSM8K with Qwen-2.5. We list the average and standard deviation across 5 runs with different seeds.

tables.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation across 5 runs with different seeds; no per-seed values or confidence interval is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: GSM8K/Qwen-2.5 summaries for Block Efficiency and Decoding Speed across Tokenwise, Blockwise and Ours. BE values are 6.40±0.10, 6.51±0.09 and 6.64±0.04; DS values are 31.52±0.06, 31.70±0.05 and 32.61±0.02.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix E Result Robustness calls Table A.1 to support stable performance; it supplements main Table 1 point estimates with repeated-run dispersion.
design_strengths: The caption defines average, standard deviation and five seeds.
Compact metric-as-row layout makes method spread easy to compare.
No legend or chromatic encoding is needed.
design_weaknesses: “Ours” is less precise than HSD, and draft/target size and temperature remain implicit.
No dataset denominator, per-seed values or confidence interval is reported.
No visual cue identifies the best mean, and the narrow table leaves unused page area.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a compact metric-row/algorithm-column appendix table for seed robustness, define the ± statistic and run count in the caption, and retain an explicit method name.

tables.label: Table A.2

caption.text: Table A.2: Comparison of task performance across model sizes and methods.

tables.uncertainty: Point accuracy only; no sample denominator, seed dispersion or interval is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: GSM8K (Accuracy) across Tokenwise and HSD for target sizes 72B, 32B and 14B. Tokenwise is 0.8213/0.8213/0.8327; HSD is 0.8517/0.8479/0.8327. Values use four decimal places.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix E Verification of Task Performance cites the table for equivalent/better accuracy and distributional fidelity; it provides the quality counterpart to efficiency Tables 1–4.
design_strengths: Explicit metric/method/model dimensions and consistent four-decimal precision make the matrix easy to scan.
The row alignment makes equality at 14B visible.
A narrow single-level header keeps this quality check compact.
design_weaknesses: Accuracy is presented without sample count or uncertainty.
“Task performance” in the caption is broader than the single GSM8K accuracy row.
No HSD bolding or explicit fidelity caveat appears in the table.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a compact model-size-by-method matrix for quality checks, but put evaluation sample/seed details and the intended fidelity interpretation in the caption.

tables.label: Table A.3

caption.text: Table A.3: Ablation on capping mechanism.

tables.uncertainty: Cells show mean ± unspecified dispersion; the PDF does not define whether ± is SD or SE or state the number of runs.
tables.data_and_statistics: GSM8K/HumanEval × HSD/HSD + Capping with ACC (%), BE and DS. ACC values are 84.40±1.75%, 80.61±0.69%, 84.96±0.93% and 82.47±1.15%; BE/DS carry corresponding ± summaries. The first two rows are HSD and the last two HSD + Capping.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix E Capped Prefix Ratio Ablation Study cites Table A.3 for the role of the capped prefix ratio in Algorithm 2; it is a mechanism/quality trade-off check rather than a headline benchmark.
design_strengths: Accuracy and efficiency are placed on one decision surface.
Two datasets expose whether the capping trade-off is task dependent.
Dispersion-like ± values are visible rather than only point estimates.
design_weaknesses: The ± statistic and run count are undefined.
ACC/BE/DS units and directions are absent from the caption.
Method variants are not visually grouped, and no highlighting makes the trade-off easy to notice.
The short caption cannot be read independently of Appendix E prose.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a compact mechanism-ablation table that puts quality and efficiency side by side, but define abbreviations and dispersion semantics and visually separate variant groups.

tables.label: Table A.4

caption.text: Table A.4: Runtime breakdown of Blockwise and HSD.

tables.uncertainty: Mean runtime and percentage-of-total only; no per-problem variation or repeated-run dispersion is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: Nine component rows (Total, Prefill, Draft Forward, Target Forward, KV Cache Input/Output, Logits Processing, Verification, Other) compare Blockwise and HSD by mean ms/token and share of total. Total is 34.168/100.00% versus 33.788/100.00%; Verification is 0.160/0.47% versus 0.127/0.37%.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix H uses Table A.4 to support verification under 1% of runtime and HSD verification about 20% faster than Blockwise; main Table 1 provides block-efficiency/speed context.
design_strengths: Paired absolute and percentage columns expose both total cost and component attribution.
Explicit units and a bold Total make the decomposition easy to audit.
Three-decimal latency values keep small verification costs visible.
design_weaknesses: No variability or per-problem denominator is shown.
Hardware, quantization and 100-problem workload conditions are not in the caption.
Two percentage columns imply precision without uncertainty, and the table sits above a large unused final-page area.
tables.reusable_pattern: Pair absolute latency with within-run percentage decomposition for each method, retain a bold total and explicit units, and put workload/hardware/variance in the caption or adjacent note.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes the HSD method interface; Figure 2 supplies a concrete GSM8K generated-prefix example; Table 1 carries the Qwen2.5 headline comparison; Table 2 extends it to 11-candidate multi-draft; Table 3 tests temperature and draft length; Table 4 tests LLaMA-family and EAGLE-3 integration. Appendix Figure A.1 connects expected full-draft acceptance theory to data, while Tables A.1–A.4 cover repeated-run robustness, accuracy/fidelity, capping and runtime. Figure A.1 is physically present even though the supplied reading inventory omits it.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use Figure/Table [label]: followed by a descriptive title. Figure 1 bolds its title; most captions describe setup/comparison rather than state a numerical conclusion. Figure A.1 is tied to the appendix acceptance term, and Table A.1 most clearly defines an uncertainty aggregation. Model, hardware and denominator details usually remain in surrounding prose.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Main tables group Block Efficiency and Decoding Speed with model scales or dataset/condition headers; composite Tables 3–4 use subpanel titles. Appendix tables mostly use one-level headers. BE, DS, ACC and N/A are not uniformly defined in captions, and Table A.3 leaves its ± statistic unspecified.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1 maps §§4–5/Algorithm 2’s backward hierarchical resampling interface; Figure 2 grounds §5.4’s token example; Table 1 gives headline results; Table 2 tests multi-draft compatibility via Appendix G/Algorithm 3; Table 3 varies temperature and draft length; Table 4 tests cross-family/EAGLE integration; Figure A.1 visualizes Appendix D’s acceptance-probability mechanism; Tables A.1–A.4 close robustness, fidelity, capping and cost boundaries.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: The main text points to Appendix E for extended experiments and Appendix H for runtime. Appendix A–D provide the theoretical/expected-length basis for Figure A.1; Appendix F contains implementation listings; Appendix G describes RRS integration; Appendix H supplies Table A.4. The appendix extends each main claim family rather than introducing a separate visual grammar.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Body/captions use Nimbus Roman No9 L at about 10 pt, main tables compress to about 7 pt, and appendix tables return to about 8–10 pt. Figure 1’s Palatino/Calibri/Times/Symbol mix, Figure 2’s monospace output and Figure A.1’s raster plotting type create local mismatches that remain functionally legible.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Figure 2 and all tables are grayscale; Figure 1 and Figure A.1 use unrelated local categorical palettes. No color role, such as HSD versus baseline, persists across figures and tables, so method identity must be re-learned in each object.

most_reusable_patterns: Double-column method-interface diagram with direct labels, local legend and explicit line/shape semantics for accepted, rejected and resampled states.
Two-level grouped result tables that put efficiency metrics and model/dataset conditions on one comparison surface, with explicit proposal-row emphasis.
Side-by-side ablation panels sharing a method row key and metric hierarchy.
Appendix tables separating repeated-run dispersion, quality/fidelity, mechanism trade-offs and runtime decomposition.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 for the backward hierarchical scan and one-resample method contract.
Table 1 for the headline BE/DS comparison across three datasets and target scales.
Table 3 for factor ablations, despite the target-model-size caption mismatch.
Table 4 for LLaMA/EAGLE-3 scope and explicit N/A handling.
Figure A.1 for the theory-to-data acceptance-probability bridge that the original reading inventory missed.
failure_patterns: Reading inventory omits the actual Appendix Figure A.1; PDF-first reconciliation is required for complete coverage.
Explicit code repository has no validated paper-specific plotting/table/LaTeX source, and the generic chain-of-thought-hub notebook must not be attributed to this paper.
Figure 1 relies heavily on color for token-state semantics and mixes imported diagram fonts; Figure A.1 uses another uncaptioned palette.
Main tables are dense and report point estimates/relative gains without run dispersion; Table A.3 shows ± values without defining the statistic or run count.

Captions are predominantly descriptive and leave model conditions, denominators and stochastic/precision caveats to prose; Table 3 names a target-size ablation not visibly present and includes the “Hierarchicial” typo.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: A colorful method schematic and a monochrome GSM8K output panel introduce HSD, after which dense grouped tables carry headline efficiency, multi-draft, ablation and integration claims, with a small appendix acceptance chart and focused robustness/fidelity/cost tables supplying the mechanism and audit trail.
